title: Cross-stitch pride flag bookmark
subtitle: A six-stripe rainbow bookmark on 14-count white Aida
excerpt: A long narrow bookmark worked in the six-stripe rainbow sequence on 14-count white Aida. The design is approximately 20 by 110 stitches and finishes at roughly 3.5 by 20 cm. A small heart at each end frames the stripe panel. A ribbon loop threaded through the top makes a neat functional finish.
sourceNotes: Original design. Bookmarks are a standard format for beginner cross-stitch projects in UK needlework publishing. The six-stripe rainbow design follows the Gilbert Baker 1978 flag sequence.

content.text: A bookmark is one of the fastest complete cross-stitch projects. The narrow width keeps the stitch count small; the length gives satisfying visible progress. The stripe pattern is entirely cross-stitch fill with no back-stitch needed for the main body.

items.label: Hoop
items.value: No hoop needed — work in hand or in a small 10 cm hoop moved along the strip

items.label: Notions
items.value: 7 cm length of narrow ribbon for loop; lightweight interfacing for backing; fabric glue or iron-on hem tape

content.text: Work a small heart motif in 3721 at the top of the design, approximately 10 by 8 stitches. Leave two blank rows of Aida above the heart for the ribbon loop.
Each stripe is the full 20-stitch width of the bookmark and 15 rows deep. Work red first, then orange, yellow, green, blue, violet downward. The six stripes together make a 90-row panel.
Repeat the heart motif at the base of the design to close the bookmark shape.
Trim the Aida to a two-hole border.
Trim the Aida to two holes beyond the outer stitches on all four sides.
Iron lightweight interfacing to the back.
Cut interfacing to match the trimmed Aida. Iron onto the reverse to stiffen the bookmark and prevent fraying.
Fold and attach the ribbon loop.
Fold the ribbon in half and sandwich the folded end between the Aida and a strip of plain cotton backing fabric at the top edge. Glue or hand-stitch to close the top.
